details: Measured 27 Oct: the notes change (branch wt/owner-notes, not merged) ran its migration with `relay queue note` from the worktree; the lander put 30+ commits on master that add a `notes` key to items, while master's code does not know the key yet. Right after, `relay queue check` on master reported "unknown key notes" for each such item (for example what-the-owner-says-about-an-item-stays-in-it.json), so master's queue check stayed red until the code merges, and a gate or hook on master in that window could refuse unrelated work. The lander's rule checks only that one file under .relay/queue/ changes, not that the default branch's own code accepts the new record.
failing_case: From a worktree whose relay_queue.py adds a new item key, `relay queue note <slug> ...` lands on master; then `relay queue check` run with master's code fails with 'unknown key notes'.
pass_cases: The lander validates the record with the default branch's schema before it lands, and refuses with the next step (merge the code first, or land from the default branch) when that schema rejects it.
A record master's code accepts still lands at once, as today.
A test in a temporary repository shows the refusal and fails with the check disabled.
reason: tests/test_queue_land_ahead.py:31 refusal test passes at head, fails at e5e3eac (Refused not raised).
findings.summary: A queue landing writes fields master's code rejects

details: CONFIRMED by reading: master_with_old_schema copies every lib/*.py and *.toml of the worktree and string-replaces one marker.
The test is right today but tied to the exact text of one line other branches (wt/majority, wt/precheck) may touch.
failing_case: A later change adds a key after "notes" in ORDER (lib/relay_queue.py:51), or reflows that line: the marker
'"dropped_at", "dropped_why", "notes")' no longer occurs once, assertEqual(old.count(marker), 1) fails, and all three tests
of the file fail (master_with_old_schema is used by two; the import of the real lib copy is used by them too) although
the lander is still right. Expected: the test keeps passing as long as the lander refuses what the default branch's code rejects.
fix_hint: Put a small stub lib/relay_queue.py on the default branch whose parse(slug, text) returns problems ["unknown key notes"]
when the JSON has `notes` and [] otherwise; drop the copy-and-patch of the real lib.
pass_cases: 1. Default branch carries a lib/relay_queue.py whose parse rejects the key `notes`; `rq.note` from the scratch repo -> Refused
containing the default branch's reason and "merge the code first"; master unchanged; no wt/queue-* branch.
2. Same default branch; `rq.set_ip` (no new key) -> lands, ip 40.
4. ORDER in lib/relay_queue.py gains a key after "notes" -> cases 1-3 still pass unchanged.
reason: tests/test_queue_land_ahead.py:31 uses a stub lib on master, no ORDER marker; accept (45) and no-lib (52) cases pass.
findings.summary: the refusal test patches a copy of the real lib by a text marker, so any change to the ORDER tuple's tail breaks it
